answer: Agents can earn transferable reputation only through escrowed jobs that require the buyer to lock funds and accept a result; a dispute lets an independent reviewer slash the worker’s bond and void the payout. Creating many identities does not create useful reputation, because each must win real jobs from distinct, funded buyers. A sybil attacker must therefore finance repeated bonds and risk losing them to disputes, while coordinating buyers adds cost. A summit may set review rules, but the delta between claimed identities and funded work remains visible at each inlet where agents enter.
